title: A shift of a K-injective complex is K-injective
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and $I$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal A$ which is K-injective, i.e. $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M,I)=0$ in the homotopy category for every acyclic complex $M$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $n\in\mathbf Z$ let $I[n]$ be the shifted complex, $(I[n])^r=I^{r+n}$, $d_{I[n]}=(-1)^nd_I$. Then $I[n]$ is K-injective for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ (and conversely, $I$ is K-injective if $I[n]$ is). Moreover, if $s:K\to I$ is a K-injective resolution (a quasi-isomorphism into a K-injective complex), then $s[n]:K[n]\to I[n]$, $(s[n])^r=s^{r+n}$, is a K-injective resolution of $K[n]$.

source.place: Definition 070H (definition-K-injective, line 9620) and the remark after it (line 9624: Hom_{K(A)}(M[i],I)=0 for all i, the translate of an acyclic complex being acyclic), which gives Hom_{K(A)}(M,I[n])=Hom_{K(A)}(M[-n],I)=0; quasi-isomorphisms are stable under shift since H^r(K[n])=H^{r+n}(K)
